candidate_relations.reason: Congenital CMV infection is the same diagnostic object as congenital cytomegalovirus infection.
Congenital toxoplasmosis is a related TORCH infection with incompatible parasite identity; maternal toxoplasma serology was negative.
Genetic disorder is a nonspecific alternative after a negative thrombophilia workup, not congenital CMV.
Intracranial hemorrhage was the fetal-ultrasound impression of the destructive lesion, not the CMV diagnosis.
Germinolytic cyst is a described imaging sequela, not congenital CMV itself.
Porencephaly is the destructive cystic sequela of fetal brain injury from CMV.
Microcephaly with simplified gyration/polymicrogyria is a brain manifestation of congenital CMV.
Vein of Galen malformation was not present on postnatal MRI.
Schizencephaly is a different migrational cleft malformation not diagnosed here.
Cerebral palsy is a possible later motor consequence, not the congenital infection.
Cytomegalovirus infection names the virus but omits the required congenital/perinatal state.
Cerebral dysgenesis is a parent description of the migrational injury missing CMV.

case_quality_flags: Maternal CMV IgM was negative at 11 weeks; congenital CMV is still the reference despite incomplete virologic confirmation in the excerpt
